newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pioneer sees better result in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pioneer sees better result in 97/98.

text.p: Building products and petrol refinery group Pioneer International Ltd should record stronger earnings in the 1997/98 fiscal year, the company's managing director, John Schubert said on Wednesday.
"I think we are going to see improving profits for the group in 1997/98," Schubert told a news conference in Sydney.
Schubert said the company was starting to see what it expected to be a significant improvement for its Australian building products business.
"In addition we are going to see continuing growth in Asia and the benefits of our capital expenditure program (in Europe and America) that is well on the way," Schubert said.
Pioneer earlier announced a net profit of A$112.7 million for the six months to December 31, down 16 percent compared with the previous corresponding first half.
The company said it expected that its second half would be weaker than its first half and that its year earnings would be materially below earnings for the previous year.
Schubert said Pioneer was on track to spend A$250 million on capital expenditure this financial year to expand its core building materials operations around the world.

He said the company had developed or acquired new quarries in the U.K., Israel, Spain, the Czech Republic, Hong Kong and Thailand and had expanded its pre-mix concrete activities in the Czech Republic, Texas, Thailand and Malaysia.

Schubert said the company was evaluating the possibility of selling its 50 percent stake in its Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (Ampol) petrol refining and marketing joint venture with Caltex Australia Ltd.
Pioneer's review of the Ampol stake had only begun in the last month and was partly triggered by the investment's unsatisfactory return on shareholders funds, Schubert said.
Schubert said the company would only sell its stake if the price received added value to the company for its shareholders.
"We are not setting ourselves a specific (sell) date, we would expect that it will take several months. It is a large investment," he said.
Schubert said the Ampol merger with Caltex had already yielded much of the synergistics benefits anticipated, and Pioneer saw these benefits ultimately at about A$600 million.

"Our growth really needs to be core businesses of concrete and quarries and cement into tied markets. We will add most value to our shareholders by concentrating quite narrowly on our product focus but having a broad geographic focus," he said.
Apart from the possible sale of its Ampol stake, Pioneer had a war chest of about A$500 million to make one or major major acquisitions, Schubert said.
If it accessed these funds, Pioneer's gearing level would rise to about 60 percent from its current level of 31 percent, he said.
